import MumfordLib.SingularSmallCochains
import MumfordLib.SingularCohomologyCircleIntersection

/-!
# Acyclic small cochains for the two-chart circle cover

Both punctured-circle charts and their intersection have zero positive-degree
singular cohomology. Correcting and gluing their primitives proves that the
cochains on simplices contained in either chart are acyclic above degree one.
Every singular cocycle in these degrees has a cohomologous representative
vanishing on all such small simplices.

This is the small-chain circle calculation for Mumford, Chapter I, Section 1,
p. 3. The passage to all singular cochains requires subdivision and is not
asserted here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

noncomputable section

open CategoryTheory

namespace Mumford.Analytic

/-- The two antipodal punctured-circle charts form an open cover. -/
theorem circle_antipodal_charts_open_cover (v : Circle) :
    IsOpen ({v}ᶜ : Set Circle) ∧ IsOpen ({-v}ᶜ : Set Circle) ∧
      ({v}ᶜ ∪ {-v}ᶜ : Set Circle) = Set.univ := by
  refine ⟨isClosed_singleton.isOpen_compl, isClosed_singleton.isOpen_compl, ?_⟩
  apply Set.eq_univ_of_forall
  intro x
  by_cases h : x = v
  · right
    simpa [h] using (Circle.neg_ne_self v).symm
  · exact Or.inl h

/-- A circle cocycle on simplices contained in either antipodal chart has a
primitive in every degree at least two. -/
theorem circleSmallCochain_exists_primitive (v : Circle) (n : ℕ)
    (φ : IntegralSimplicialCochain
      (singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ ⊔
        singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {-v}ᶜ :
          (TopCat.toSSet.obj (TopCat.of Circle)).Subcomplex) (n + 2))
    (hφ : simplicialCochainDifferential _ (n + 2) φ = 0) :
    ∃ ψ, simplicialCochainDifferential _ (n + 1) ψ = φ :=
  smallSingularCochain_two_exists_primitive (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ {-v}ᶜ n
    (singularCocycle_puncturedCircle_exists_primitive v)
    (singularCocycle_puncturedCircle_exists_primitive (-v))
    (singularCocycle_circleChartIntersection_exists_primitive v) φ hφ

set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false in
/-- Every circle cocycle above degree one is cohomologous to a cochain that
vanishes on every simplex contained in one of the two charts. -/
theorem singularCocycle_circle_exists_representative_zero_on_small
    (v : Circle) (n : ℕ) (φ : singularCocycles (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 2)) :
    ∃ ψ : IntegralSingularCochain (TopCat.of Circle) (n + 1),
      simplicialCochainPullback
        (singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ ⊔
          singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {-v}ᶜ).ι (n + 2)
        (φ.1 - singularCochainCoboundary ψ) = 0 := by
  let A := singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {v}ᶜ ⊔
    singularSubset (TopCat.of Circle) {-v}ᶜ
  have hφ : simplicialCochainDifferential (TopCat.toSSet.obj (TopCat.of Circle))
      (n + 2) φ.1 = 0 := φ.2
  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := circleSmallCochain_exists_primitive v n
    (simplicialCochainPullback A.ι (n + 2) φ.1) (by
      rw [← simplicialCochainPullback_differential, hφ, map_zero])
  obtain ⟨ψ, hψ⟩ := simplicialCochainPullback_subcomplex_surjective A (n + 1) α
  refine ⟨ψ, ?_⟩
  have hd : simplicialCochainPullback A.ι (n + 2) (singularCochainCoboundary ψ) =
      simplicialCochainDifferential A (n + 1)
        (simplicialCochainPullback A.ι (n + 1) ψ) :=
    simplicialCochainPullback_differential A.ι ψ
  rw [map_sub, hd, hψ, hα, sub_self]

end Mumford.Analytic
